stemMd: A charity may use donated money for administration only when the donor explicitly permits it. A donor gives unrestricted permission to use a gift for any lawful charity purpose. Administrative payroll is a lawful charity purpose. Which is best supported?

options.label: A
options.textMd: No further law can restrict the payroll expenditure.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Payroll is the charity's most valuable purpose.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every donation may be used for administration.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The charity must spend the entire gift on payroll.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The stated donor restriction does not prevent using this gift for administrative payroll.

explanationMd: The gift expressly covers every lawful charity purpose, and payroll is stipulated to be one. That satisfies the donor-permission condition. It neither mandates that expenditure nor removes other possible legal requirements.

distractorRationale.d: Permission is not a spending obligation.
distractorRationale.b: Lawfulness does not establish comparative value.
distractorRationale.a: The rule addresses donor permission, not every external constraint.
